data.long_meaning: The name Tessaiah comes from the Hebrew language, where it is composed of two parts: 'Tes' meaning 'God' and 'Yah' meaning 'salvation'. This name is a strong reminder of God's presence and protection throughout one's life. In Christian tradition, it is a symbol of faith and trust in the Lord's saving grace. The name Tessaiah carries the meaning “God is my salvation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tessaiah usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my salvation and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: טסאיָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טסאיָה הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'האלוקים יפיח חיים בנצחיות וישועה'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'טס' שפירושו 'להפיח' ו'איָה' שפירושו 'אלוקים הוא ישועה'. השם נגזר מהשורש 'נפח' שפירושו 'להביא חיים' והוא קשור לנושא הישועה והחיים הנצחיים.

in_greek.name: Τεσσαΐας
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι σωτηρία και αιώνια ζωή
in_greek.long_meaning: Τεσσαΐας είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι σωτηρία και αιώνια ζωή'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'Τεσσα' που σημαίνει 'τέσσερις' ή 'σωτηρία' και 'Άς' που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Το όνομα σχετίζεται με την έννοια της σωτηρίας και της αιώνιας ζωής.

in_latin.name: Tessaiah
in_latin.meaning: Deus est salus et vita aeterna
in_latin.long_meaning: Tessaiah est nomen hebraicum quod significat 'Deus est salus et vita aeterna'. Nomen componitur ex duobus verbis: 'Tes' quod significat 'spirare' et 'Aiah' quod significat 'Deus est salus'. Nomen derivatur a radix 'napaḥ' quod significat 'vitam afferre' et coniungitur cum conceptu salvationis et vitae aeternae.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Tesseus or Tissaiah is mentioned as a descendant of King Saul through his son Jonathan and grandson Merib-baal. Merib-baal was killed by the Gibeonites, leading to a famine in Israel. The prophet Samuel led the people to seek God's forgiveness and instructed them to go to Gibeon to offer sacrifices. Tessaiah led the return to Gibeon with his sons, joining the assembly of elders and priests to offer the sacrifices. (1 Samuel 14:32-34)

Tessaiah is also mentioned in the New Testament, in the Gospel of Matthew (17:24-27), as a tax collector who approached Jesus and his disciples while they were in Capernaum. Tessaiah recognized Jesus as the Son of God and asked him how to fulfill the temple tax. Jesus instructed him to go to the sea, cast a hook and take the first fish that bit, open its mouth, and find a shekel inside. When Tessaiah did this, he was amazed and fell at Jesus' feet, acknowledging him as the Son of God.
